model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) in percentage (%) as a function of the co-occurrence number, with the x-axis representing the co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10 to 1000. The y-axis represents accuracy, ranging from 40% to 65%. Five different methods are compared: Base (black circles, solid line), MEND (brown triangles, dashed line), FT (blue triangles, dashed line), IKE (red triangles, dashed line), and ROME (green squares, solid line). The Base method starts at approximately 41% accuracy and remains relatively flat, ending at around 45%. MEND starts at about 45% and increases to roughly 56%. FT begins at about 41% and rises to approximately 48%. IKE starts at around 44% and increases to about 50%. ROME starts at approximately 52% and shows a steady increase, reaching about 65% at the highest co-occurrence number.
